questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and Correcting Statements

subQuestions.questionText:
Market equilibrium occurs when the …
A. supply and the demand are not equal.
B. supply is more than the demand.
C. market supply is equal to the market demand.
D. demand is lower than the supply.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - market supply is equal to the market demand (2 marks)
At equilibrium the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded, so there is no shortage or surplus and the price is stable.

options.A: supply and the demand are not equal.
options.B: supply is more than the demand.
options.C: market supply is equal to the market demand.
options.D: demand is lower than the supply.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is NOT a component of selling:
A. Management is sales-volume oriented.
B. The emphasis is on the consumer's needs.
C. The focus is on the seller's needs.
D. The emphasis is on the agricultural product.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - The emphasis is on the consumer's needs (2 marks)
Emphasis on consumer needs is part of the marketing concept. Selling focuses on the product, the seller's needs and sales volume.

options.B: The emphasis is on the consumer's needs.
options.C: The focus is on the seller's needs.
options.D: The emphasis is on the agricultural product.

subQuestions.questionText:
An operational production plan in a business plan focuses on the …
A. number and type of employees.
B. recruitment of suitable personnel.
C. summary of the enterprise details.
D. monitoring of performance and ensuring quality control.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - monitoring of performance and ensuring quality control (2 marks)
The operational (production) plan sets out how production will be carried out, monitored and controlled to meet quality standards.

options.D: monitoring of performance and ensuring quality control.

subQuestions.questionText:
The descriptions below address opportunities that could be realised through the SWOT analysis.
(i) New markets opening to increase sales
(ii) New technologies to improve efficiency of the business
(iii) Limited resources to farm effectively
(iv) Access to a grant from government
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (ii) and (iv)
B. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (iii) and (iv)
D. (i), (ii) and (iii)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Opportunities are favourable external factors. Limited resources (iii) is an internal weakness, not an opportunity.

subQuestions.questionText:
The part of the expenditure of a farming enterprise which is NOT influenced by the level of production:
A. Demand costs
B. Fixed costs
C. Supply costs
D. Variable costs
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Fixed costs (2 marks)
Fixed costs (e.g. rent, licences, depreciation) stay the same regardless of how much is produced. Variable costs change with the level of production.

subQuestions.questionText:
The type of labour hired solely to erect a kraal:
A. Permanent
B. Seasonal
C. Full-time
D. Casual
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Casual (2 marks)
Casual labour is hired for a specific short once-off task, such as building a kraal, and is not tied to a season or to permanent employment.

subQuestions.questionText:
The action by a farmer to address undercapitalisation on the farm:
A. Keep old non-viable tractors
B. Pay higher wages
C. Hire specific machinery
D. Invest more money in the bank
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Hire specific machinery (2 marks)
Undercapitalisation means too little capital is invested in the business. Hiring machinery instead of buying it lets the farmer get the work done without a large capital outlay.

options.D: Invest more money in the bank

subQuestions.questionText:
The skill that enables the manager to protect the business from monetary losses:
A. Financial management
B. Decision-making
C. Interpersonal
D. Problem-solving
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Financial management (2 marks)
Financial management skills (budgeting, record keeping, cash-flow control) protect the business from monetary losses.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following statements are about Mendel's laws of inheritance:
(i) Pairs of alleles separate randomly during meiosis.
(ii) Pairs of alleles arrange themselves dependently of each other.
(iii) Pairs of alleles arrange themselves independently of each other.
(iv) In a heterozygous state a dominant allele influences the physical appearance of an organism.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
A. (i), (ii) and (iv)
B. (ii), (iii) and (iv)
C. (i), (ii) and (iii)
D. (i), (iii) and (iv)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
(i) is the law of segregation, (iii) is the law of independent assortment and (iv) is the law of dominance. Statement (ii) contradicts independent assortment.

subQuestions.questionText:
An example of a heterozygous genotype for the colour of flowers:
A. FRFR
B. FWFW
C. FRFW
D. FBFB
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - FRFW (2 marks)
A heterozygous genotype has two different alleles. FRFW carries one red allele and one white allele; the other options are all homozygous.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term in COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A form of sustainable agricultural marketing that is responding to the increasing environmental concerns.
COLUMN B options: A. retailer  B. internal  C. agrimarketing  D. X-rays  E. external  F. broker  G. fixed capital  H. green marketing  I. movable capital  J. nitric acid
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: H - green marketing (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term in COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: The type of buyer working as an agent for commission.
COLUMN B options: A. retailer  B. internal  C. agrimarketing  D. X-rays  E. external  F. broker  G. fixed capital  H. green marketing  I. movable capital  J. nitric acid
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: F - broker (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term in COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Medium-term investment assets.
COLUMN B options: A. retailer  B. internal  C. agrimarketing  D. X-rays  E. external  F. broker  G. fixed capital  H. green marketing  I. movable capital  J. nitric acid
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: I - movable capital (2 marks)
Movable capital (machinery, vehicles, livestock) is a medium-term investment asset, financed over a few years.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term in COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Forces originating from the farm which have an impact on farm management.
COLUMN B options: A. retailer  B. internal  C. agrimarketing  D. X-rays  E. external  F. broker  G. fixed capital  H. green marketing  I. movable capital  J. nitric acid
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - internal (2 marks)
Internal forces originate within the farm business and can be controlled by management.

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a word/term in COLUMN B that matches the description in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: Damages the DNA molecule and causes it to break.
COLUMN B options: A. retailer  B. internal  C. agrimarketing  D. X-rays  E. external  F. broker  G. fixed capital  H. green marketing  I. movable capital  J. nitric acid
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - X-rays (2 marks)
X-rays are a physical mutagen that damages the DNA molecule and can cause chromosome breaks.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
The marketing system where the price of a product is decided upon by the government.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Controlled marketing (1 mark for term; 2 marks allocated to the item)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A practice where uneconomic pieces of farmland are put together to increase productivity.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Consolidation (of land) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A type of dominance where none of the parent characteristics are visible in the offspring.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Incomplete dominance (2 marks)
In incomplete dominance the heterozygote shows a blended, intermediate phenotype rather than either parent's characteristic.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
A technique where an electric current is passed through a solution containing the desired genes.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Electroporation (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description:
An organism with more than two sets of chromosomes.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Polyploidy (polyploid organism) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Price monopoly is the setting of the price of goods and services with no bargaining allowed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Price fixing (1 mark)
Setting a price with no bargaining allowed is price fixing. A price monopoly is where a single seller controls the market.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
The money which is paid back to a financial institution over and above the money borrowed is credit.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Interest (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
Estimated breeding value is the use of statistics to analyse biological data.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Biometrics (1 mark)
The use of statistics to analyse biological data is biometrics. Estimated breeding value is a prediction of an animal's genetic merit as a parent.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
The occurrence in chickens of an extra toe after it has been absent for many generations is an example of prepotency.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Atavism (throwback) (1 mark)
The reappearance of an ancestral characteristic after many generations is atavism.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED word(s) to make the statement TRUE:
A small piece of the DNA that carries hereditary information of a characteristic is known as a chromosome.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Gene (1 mark)
A gene is a segment of DNA that codes for a characteristic. A chromosome is a long, coiled DNA molecule carrying many genes.

questions.title: Section B, Question 2: Agricultural Management and Marketing

subQuestions.questionText:
A graph in the question paper shows the quantities (in tons) of two agricultural products (Product 1 and Product 2) available in a market over a period of six months. Product 2 stays constant at about 20 tons every month; Product 1 varies from month to month.
Indicate the quantity of product 1 that was available in month 3.
subQuestions.memoText: 30 tons (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the product (from the six-month availability graph) that shows constant availability over the six-month period.
subQuestions.memoText: Product 2 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the problem that may occur in the market with product 2 if the demand is 20 tons.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• There will be a surplus / spoilage / storage costs (supply of about 20 tons roughly equals demand, so any excess is wasted)
• The price of the product will drop

subQuestions.questionText: Name the factor that may hamper the marketing of product 1 (whose supply fluctuates greatly from month to month).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Seasonal fluctuation in production
• Perishability
• Accidents / theft
• Lack of infrastructure
• Lack of capital
• Lack of market information
• Long distances to markets

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO factors that can influence the demand of product 1 and product 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Price of the product
• Change in consumer income / buying power
• Number of consumers
• Tastes and preferences of consumers
• Price of competing / complementing / substitute products
• Range of products available
• Usefulness of the product
• Quality of the product
• Festive season / fashion
• Research
• Socio-economic factors
• Legislation
• Advertising
• Price expectations

subQuestions.questionText:
A flow chart in the question paper illustrates a MARKETING SYSTEM with three channels:
A – Products are sold to hawkers from the farm.
B – Farmers market through an agent.
C – Livestock is sold to the highest bidder.
Identify the marketing system illustrated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Free marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify channels A and B used in the marketing system in QUESTION 2.2.1 (A – products sold to hawkers from the farm; B – farmers market through an agent).
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Farm-gate marketing (1 mark)
B - Fresh produce marketing (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.2.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: State ONE advantage of channel A (farm-gate marketing) for the farmer.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): no market-chain costs / no transportation costs / no intermediaries / higher income / immediate payment.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: State ONE advantage of channel A (farm-gate marketing) for the consumer.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): products will be fresh / better quality / lower prices / consumer has bargaining power.

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE disadvantage of channel C (livestock sold to the highest bidder at auction) to sellers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Prices may be lower than the market price
• The seller may not get the expected price / less profit
• Small-scale farmers may not have money to transport animals to the auction

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario: A group of youth near a livestock farm decided to collect manure from the farm to generate biofuel used as a source of energy. They drafted a business plan, which was used to secure funding from a bank, and bought a biogas digester. An old building was used as a factory and skilled personnel were hired to run the business. The business flourished and they started to service the community.
Identify THREE phases of entrepreneurship in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE (1 mark each):
• Identifying the opportunity (collecting manure to make biofuel)
• Developing a business plan
• Resource mobilisation (securing funding, buying the digester, using the old building, hiring personnel)
• Starting and managing the enterprise (the business flourished and serviced the community)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO other reasons for drafting a business plan, except for the one in the scenario above (securing funding).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• To test the feasibility / economic viability of the business idea
• Helps to define goals
• Outlines the roles and responsibilities of individuals
• Provides time frames for completion of activities
• Provides guidelines for decision making / to compare progress
• To guide daily operations
• Helps the manager plan for capital requirements
• Provides clear strategies / objectives to follow
• To ensure effective business management
• Allows problems to be foreseen, reducing risk
• Repositions the business to deal with market changes
• To gain knowledge about marketing opportunities / competitors
• Attract investors / partners

subQuestions.label: 2.3.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate a success factor of this group which enabled them to get other people to believe in their idea and work with them.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): leadership / organisation / management / interpersonal skills / confidence.

subQuestions.label: 2.3.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate a success factor of this group which enabled them to invest in new equipment with the hope of succeeding in the business.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): risk taking / confidence / positive thinking.

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows bags of potatoes offered in a market over five weeks.
Week | Price (Rand) | Quantities offered (bags)
1 | 10 | 500
2 | 20 | 1 000
3 | 30 | 1 500
4 | 40 | 2 000
5 | 50 | 2 500
Draw a line graph showing the quantities of potatoes offered at different prices.
subQuestions.memoText:
Line graph. Marking rubric (1 mark each):
• Correct heading
• X-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Quantities, bags)
• Y-axis correctly calibrated and labelled (Price, R)
• Correct units (R and bags)
• Line graph drawn (single upward-sloping line)
• Accuracy (80%+ of points correctly plotted); the line rises steadily from (500, R10) to (2 500, R50)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the marketing law applicable to the data provided in the table above (potato quantities offered at rising prices).
subQuestions.memoText: The law of supply: the higher the price, the higher the quantity supplied; the lower the price, the lower the quantity supplied. There is a direct (positive) relationship between price and quantity supplied. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO factors, other than the price, that could have contributed to the quantities of potatoes offered.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Environmental conditions / nature (weather, climate)
• Availability of technology
• Knowledge on production
• Production costs
• Subsidies / taxation / legislation
• Number of suppliers
• Price expectation / profit margin
• Demand for the product
• Seasonal production
• Political instability
• Possibility of increasing / decreasing supply
• Stability (storability) of the product

subQuestions.questionText:
A schematic representation in the question paper shows the marketing chain stages a product passes through from the farm to the consumer: Farm → Grading → Processing → Storage → Transport → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer.
Indicate TWO costs in the schematic representation that could increase the price of a product when it reaches the consumer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Production costs
• Packaging costs
• Processing costs
• Storage costs
• Transportation / distribution costs
• Grading costs

subQuestions.label: 2.5.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the stage in the marketing chain in which the following occurs to improve the agribusiness:
(a) Installing cold rooms to prevent spoilage before transporting to the wholesaler.
subQuestions.memoText: Storage (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 2.5.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the stage in the marketing chain in which the following occurs to improve the agribusiness:
(b) Improving road infrastructure for the product to reach the processing stage.
subQuestions.memoText: Farm (the stage before grading/processing, from where the product must be moved). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the retailer can make the product known to the consumer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Advertising (radio / television / billboards / newspapers / internet / brochures / posters / flyers)
• In-store promotion
• Exhibitions / trade fairs
• Sponsorship
• Direct mailing
• Using a marketing agent
• Personal selling

subQuestions.questionText: The availability of agricultural land is limited. State TWO other economic characteristics of land.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Land is required for all production
• Land is fixed / found in a specific location
• Land is indestructible
• Land appreciates in value
• Durability
• Varies in production potential
• Restrictedness
• A passive / primary production factor
• A source of wealth (can be bought, sold or used as collateral)
• Subject to the law of diminishing returns

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the productivity of land can be improved.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Improve water management / water supply
• Restore land potential / use pesticides responsibly
• Farm the land more efficiently / consolidate uneconomic units
• Crop rotation / intercropping / rotational grazing
• Research
• Use scientific methods / technology / improve soil fertility / precision farming

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO functions associated with land as a production factor.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Asset used as collateral in obtaining loans
• Provides space for agricultural activities
• Provides food / feed for humans and animals
• Source of raw materials
• Source of minerals

subQuestions.questionText:
A graph in the question paper shows the number of people employed by a farmer (1 to 5) on the x-axis and the quantity of outputs on the y-axis. Output rises as more people are employed.
Identify the production factor illustrated in the graph above.
subQuestions.memoText: Labour (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce, from the graph above, the relationship between the number of people employed from 1 to 5 and their outputs.
subQuestions.memoText: An increase in the number of workers resulted in an increase in output (a direct / positive relationship). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO problems of labour in a farming enterprise.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Poor labour management / supervision / late arrival / theft
• Scarcity of labour / low wages
• Lack of training / skills
• HIV/AIDS or other diseases / absenteeism
• Competition from industries
• Socio-economic problems
• Labour unrest

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the farmer can improve the economic conditions of farm workers.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Pay higher wages
• Provide incentives for workers
• Pay bonuses
• Provide medical insurance / pension
• Supply farm products at reduced prices
• Enter into a partnership deal with workers
• Provide education and training

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the labour legislation that regulates the following: leave days, working hours, salaries and overtime.
subQuestions.memoText: Basic Conditions of Employment Act / BCEA (Act 75 of 1997) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the labour legislation that aims to develop and improve the competencies of labourers to operate machinery effectively.
subQuestions.memoText: Skills Development Act / SDA (Act 97 of 1998) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the labour legislation that requires farm workers to wear overalls and gumboots for their daily operations.
subQuestions.memoText: Occupational Health and Safety Act / OHSA (Act 85 of 1993) (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The table below provides information on assets and liabilities on a farm.
A. Value of the farm — R3 500 000
B. Tractor loan — R365 000
C. Value of vehicles — R275 000
D. Bank overdraft — R150 000
E. Mortgage loan — R4 200 000
F. Cash — R650 000
G. Value of buildings — R50 000
Identify an item from the table above that represents an asset.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Value of the farm (A) / Value of vehicles (C) / Cash (F) / Value of buildings (G).

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify an item from the assets and liabilities table above that represents a liability.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): Tractor loan (B) / Bank overdraft (D) / Mortgage loan (E).

subQuestions.questionText: Use a formula to calculate the net worth of the farm (using the assets and liabilities table above).
Refer to the calculation in QUESTION 3.4.2 to indicate the viability of this farming business.
subQuestions.memoText: Not viable (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason to support the answer to QUESTION 3.4.3.
subQuestions.memoText: The net worth is negative (−R240 000); the value of the assets is less than the value of the liabilities, so the business shows a loss / no profit. (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.5.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A picture in the question paper represents a farm with different farming enterprises and capital items, labelled A to F (A–C are objects on the right of the picture, D–F on the left). 
Identify the type of capital represented by item C.
subQuestions.memoText: C - Movable capital (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.5.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the type of capital represented by item B in the farm picture.
subQuestions.memoText: B - Fixed capital (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the problem of capital item F (a tractor) in the farm picture.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE (1 mark): depreciation / loses value over time / high fuel and maintenance costs.

subQuestions.label: 3.5.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Name a type of credit that is used to acquire the capital item represented by D in the farm picture.
subQuestions.memoText: D - Short-term credit (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 3.5.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name a type of credit that is used to acquire the capital item represented by E in the farm picture.
subQuestions.memoText: E - Long-term credit (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
A farming business should be well managed to be successful and to achieve the intended goals and objectives.
Define the term management.
subQuestions.memoText: Management is the effective combination and co-ordination of human, physical and financial resources (1 mark) to achieve a specific goal, usually maximising profit (1 mark). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO management principles of a business to be successful.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO (1 mark each): planning / setting goals; implementation; leading / directing; organisation / co-ordination; decision making; communication; motivation; monitoring; control.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO risk management techniques.
subQuestions.memoText:
• Diversification (1 mark)
• Risk sharing (1 mark)

questions.title: Section B, Question 4: Basic Agricultural Genetics

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
An illustration in the question paper shows the repeated crossing of farm animals, using the same bull each time to improve growth rate:
Crossing 1: Simmentaler cow × Brahman bull → Simbra heifer F1
Crossing 2: Simbra heifer F1 × Brahman bull → Simbra heifer F2
Crossing 3: Simbra heifer F2 × Brahman bull → Simbra F3
Name the breeding system represented by Crossing 1.
subQuestions.memoText: Crossing 1 - Crossbreeding (crossing two different breeds). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the breeding system represented by Crossing 3 (Simbra heifer F2, which is largely Brahman, mated back to a Brahman bull).
subQuestions.memoText: Crossing 3 - Inbreeding (grading up / breeding closely related animals of the same breed). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Define the breeding system represented by Crossing 3.
subQuestions.memoText: Inbreeding is the breeding of closely related animals. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE disadvantage of the breeding system represented by Crossing 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Leads to inbreeding depression
• Loss of genetic variation
• Increases the expression of lethal genes
• Undesired genes become more homozygous
• Undesirable characteristics / deformities can be bred into the progeny
• Leads to reduced vitality
• Less resistance to diseases
• An expensive system

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of the breeding system represented by Crossing 1 (crossbreeding).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Produces hybrid vigour / heterosis
• Development of new breeds
• Increased adaptability
• Increases genetic variation
• More resistant to pests / diseases
• Improves the performance of animals

subQuestions.questionText: Variation is caused by both internal and external factors. State TWO internal causes of variation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Mutation
• Meiosis / crossing-over / recombination of genes
• Random fertilisation

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO important aspects (importance) of variation in breeding.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Forms the basis of selection
• Improves existing breeds / cultivars
• Allows the development of new breeds / plant cultivars

subQuestions.questionText:
Match a method of selection (mass selection; family selection; progeny selection; pedigree selection) with the statement:
Animals are selected based on the records of their ancestors.
subQuestions.memoText: Pedigree selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Match a method of selection with the statement:
Selection is based on the quality of relatives of its own generation.
subQuestions.memoText: Family selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Match a method of selection with the statement:
Farm animals are selected based on individual performance.
subQuestions.memoText: Mass selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Match a method of selection with the statement:
Selection is based on the quality of the offspring.
subQuestions.memoText: Progeny selection (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A Punnett square in the question paper represents the crossing of a bull heterozygous for both characteristics (HhRW) with a heterozygous polled white cow. KEY — Characteristic 1 (horn conformation): H = polled (no horns), h = horned. Characteristic 2 (hair colour): W = white, R = red, RW = roan. The bull's gametes are HR, HW, hR (gamete 17) and hW; the cow's gametes are HW, HW, hW, hW. The 16 offspring (numbered 1–16) are: 1 HHRW, 2 HHWW, 3 HhRW, 4 HhWW, 5 HHRW, 6 HHWW, 7 HhRW, 8 HhWW, 9 HhRW, 10 HhWW, 11 hhRW, 12 hhWW, 13 HhRW, 14 HhWW, 15 hhRW, 16 hhWW.
Give the genotype of the female parent.
subQuestions.memoText: HhWW (heterozygous polled, homozygous white). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the genotype of gamete numbered 17 in the Punnett square above (one of the bull's gametes).
subQuestions.memoText: hR (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.4.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the phenotype of individual number 9 (genotype HhRW) in the Punnett square above.
subQuestions.memoText: Polled and roan (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.4.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the phenotype of individual number 16 (genotype hhWW) in the Punnett square above.
subQuestions.memoText: Horned and white (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the number of horned roan cattle (genotype hhRW) in the Punnett square above.
subQuestions.memoText: 2 (individuals 11 and 15). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the number of polled red cattle in the Punnett square above.
subQuestions.memoText: 0 — no offspring is homozygous RR (red); every offspring is either roan (RW) or white (WW). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.5.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Farm animals have sex chromosomes (gonosomes) and body chromosomes (autosomes). Horses have 64 chromosomes and goats have 60.
Indicate the number of sex chromosomes in goats.
subQuestions.memoText: 2 (1 pair). (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.5.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the number of pairs of autosomes in horses (which have 64 chromosomes in total).
subQuestions.memoText: 31 pairs. (64 chromosomes − 2 sex chromosomes = 62 autosomes = 31 pairs.) (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.5.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: If a ram (XY) is mated with an ewe (XX), indicate the percentage chance of male offspring that could be produced.
subQuestions.memoText: 50% (1 mark)

subQuestions.label: 4.5.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If a ram (XY) is mated with an ewe (XX), determine the ratio of male to female offspring.
subQuestions.memoText: 1 : 1 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows heritability of different characteristics in farm animals.
Characteristic | Heritability (%)
Milk production | 40
Eye colour | 70
Fleece weight | 20
Define the term heritability.
subQuestions.memoText: Heritability is the degree (proportion) to which a characteristic (1 mark) is determined by genetic factors rather than the environment (1 mark). (2 marks)

subQuestions.label: 4.6.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the qualitative characteristic from the heritability table above (Milk production 40%, Eye colour 70%, Fleece weight 20%).
subQuestions.memoText: Eye colour (1 mark) — it falls into distinct categories and is controlled by one or a few genes.

subQuestions.label: 4.6.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify a quantitative characteristic from the heritability table above.
subQuestions.memoText: Milk production or fleece weight (1 mark) — these show continuous variation and are controlled by many genes.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the percentage of environmental effect on milk production (heritability 40%).
subQuestions.memoText: 60% (100% − 40% heritability). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the relationship between heritability and the estimated breeding value (EBV).
subQuestions.memoText: The higher the heritability of a trait, the higher (more reliable) the estimated breeding value; the lower the heritability, the lower (less reliable) the estimated breeding value. Heritability and EBV are directly related. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Genetic modification is the technique of changing the characteristics of an organism by inserting genes from another organism into the DNA of the original organism.
State TWO advantages of genetic modification over traditional breeding methods.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• It is precise
• It is faster
• It is not limited to organisms of the same species

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO negative effects of GM crops on the environment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Leads to the development of super weeds
• Beneficial insects can be killed
• Leads to the excessive use of herbicides / pollution
• Reduces biodiversity
